import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set style
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-darkgrid')
sns.set_palette("husl")

# Create figure with subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(18, 12))

# 1. Price distribution by brand (top 10 brands)
ax1 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 1)
top_brands = df['brand'].value_counts().head(10).index
brand_data = df[df['brand'].isin(top_brands)]
sns.boxplot(data=brand_data, x='brand', y='price_usd', order=top_brands)
ax1.set_xlabel('Brand', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_title('Price Distribution by Top 10 Brands', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')
ax1.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 2. Megapixels vs Price by Sensor Type
ax2 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 2)
sns.scatterplot(data=df, x='megapixels', y='price_usd', hue='sensor_type', 
                alpha=0.7, s=60, edgecolor='w', linewidth=0.5)
ax2.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_title('Megapixels vs Price by Sensor Type', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')
ax2.legend(title='Sensor Type', title_fontsize=10, fontsize=9)

# 3. Camera count by body type
ax3 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 3)
body_counts = df['body_type'].value_counts()
colors = plt.cm.Set3(np.linspace(0, 1, len(body_counts)))
bars = ax3.bar(body_counts.index, body_counts.values, color=colors, edgecolor='black')
ax3.set_xlabel('Body Type', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_ylabel('Number of Cameras', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_title('Camera Distribution by Body Type', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')
ax3.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# Add count labels on bars
for bar in bars:
    height = bar.get_height()
    ax3.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2., height + 5,
             f'{int(height)}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=9)

# 4. Weight vs Price with 4K video capability
ax4 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 4)
video_labels = {0: 'No 4K Video', 1: 'Has 4K Video'}
df['video_label'] = df['has_video_4k'].map(video_labels)
sns.scatterplot(data=df, x='weight_grams', y='price_usd', hue='video_label',
                alpha=0.6, s=50, style='video_label', markers=['o', 's'])
ax4.set_xlabel('Weight (grams)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax4.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax4.set_title('Weight vs Price by 4K Video Capability', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')
ax4.legend(title='4K Video', title_fontsize=10, fontsize=9)

# 5. Average price by model year
ax5 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 5)
yearly_avg = df.groupby('model_year')['price_usd'].mean().reset_index()
sns.lineplot(data=yearly_avg, x='model_year', y='price_usd', 
             marker='o', linewidth=2.5, markersize=8, color='darkred')
ax5.set_xlabel('Model Year', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax5.set_ylabel('Average Price (USD)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax5.set_title('Average Camera Price by Model Year', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')
ax5.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# 6. Max ISO distribution by sensor type
ax6 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 6)
sns.violinplot(data=df, x='sensor_type', y='max_iso', inner='quartile', cut=0)
ax6.set_xlabel('Sensor Type', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax6.set_ylabel('Max ISO', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax6.set_title('Max ISO Distribution by Sensor Type', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')
ax6.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
ax6.set_yscale('log')

# Adjust layout and add main title
plt.suptitle('Digital Camera Market Analysis: Specifications and Pricing Trends', 
             fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150, facecolor='white')
plt.close()
